test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If a + b = 56 and (a - b)² = 496, find the value of product of a and b.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the standard algebraic identity: 4ab = (a + b)² − (a − b)²

Substitute the given values directly into the formula:

4ab = 56² − 496

4ab = 3136 − 496 = 2640

ab = 2640 ÷ 4 = 660

**∴ The correct answer is 660.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + b = 56

(a − b)² = 496

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

Subtracting the second equation from the first, we get:

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ (56)² − 496 = 4ab

⇒ 3136 − 496 = 4ab

⇒ 2640 = 4ab

⇒ ab = 2640 ÷ 4

⇒ ab = 660

**∴ The correct answer is 660.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). This identity is directly useful when the sum of the squares of two variables is required.

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). This is a foundational factorization rule widely used in simplifying algebraic fractions and equations.

Cubic Identities

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²). Frequently tested alongside square identities in competitive exams.
